Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: The Tasteful Agent: Measuring and Improving Taste in Long-Horizon Tasks
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Wenbo Pan, Zhichao Liu, Shujie Liu, Jingying Zeng, Chin-Yew Lin
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The paper introduces Taste-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate and enhance the decision-making "taste" of LLM agents in long-horizon tasks, revealing significant challenges and training potential.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: LLM agents increasingly work on long-horizon tasks, and the decisions they make along the way, such as which hypothesis to test or which implementation to build on, determine the outcome of the whole run. Making these decisions well is becoming a key capability for both engineering and research agents. We refer to the ability to make good long-horizon decisions as the taste of an agent. While existing benchmarks measure the end-to-end success of agents on long-horizon tasks, none of them measures the taste of an agent. To address this problem, we build Taste-Bench, a benchmark of taste questions constructed automatically from trajectories that agents produced in engineering and research tasks. Each question presents a decision fork, a point in a trajectory where multiple directions are available and one of them leads to a better outcome, and the evaluated model chooses among these directions without seeing what happens after the fork. We mine these forks automatically from parallel attempts at the same task and from detours inside a single trajectory, without needing human annotation. We evaluate frontier models on Taste-Bench and find that the best model answers only 59.7% of the questions correctly. We further find that forks whose deciding evidence appears later in the trajectory are much harder for every model, and that a larger reasoning budget does not improve the accuracy. Finally, we show that taste can be trained. We distill the judgment of a teacher that has seen the outcome into a student model, and the student makes better decisions on unseen tasks and improves end-to-end success on held-out SWE-bench Pro tasks.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: LiFR v2: Completion-Augmented Event Propagation for High-Rate Dense Prediction
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Tao Wan, Xiaoshan Wu, Yifei Yu, Bo Wang, Xiaoyang Lyu
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: LiFR v2 enhances high-rate dense prediction by integrating RGB keyframes and event data through a novel framework, achieving superior performance in semantic segmentation and depth estimation.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: High-rate dense perception in dynamic environments is limited by the low update rate of RGB cameras, as rapid scene changes can occur between frames. Event cameras offer temporally dense but spatially sparse measurements, complementary to spatially dense RGB observations. Direct fusion cannot fully exploit this complementarity, while event-guided propagation fails on newly appearing or disoccluded regions without valid RGB support. We present LiFR v2, a unified propagation-completion-memory framework for causal anytime and streaming dense prediction from an RGB keyframe and events. LiFR v2 introduces an Event-Guided Completion Module (EGCM) to recover task-relevant representations where propagation is unsupported, and a History Retrieval Module (HRM) to reuse completed representations across successive queries. The framework supports semantic segmentation, monocular depth estimation, and multi-task dense prediction, and we further introduce SHF-Emerge to evaluate rapid object emergence and disocclusion. It also exceeds 100 FPS for both segmentation and depth, demonstrating accurate and efficient high-rate perception beyond RGB frame rates.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Fysiverse-3D-Vision Technical Report: Generating Executable 3D Worlds from Images through Unified Spatial Reasoning
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Dingkang Yang, Yizhou Liu, Wendong Cheng, Zizhi Chen, Shunli Wang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Fysiverse-3D-Vision introduces a unified framework for generating executable 3D scenes from images, enhancing spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction for interactive content creation.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Generative models have advanced image-conditioned 3D content creation, yet generating controllable and executable 3D scenes from a single image remains challenging. They struggle to jointly model object semantics, metric geometry, and scene-level spatial relationships, which are essential for interactive editing, physical simulation, and embodied applications. We establish a shared representation where spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction mutually enhance each other, allowing object layouts to be inferred beyond the constraints of individual asset generators. Our model integrates textual supervision, semantic visual cues, and geometric representations within a unified Transformer to capture scene context, metric geometry, and object-level interactions. An object-conditioned layout module performs cross-attention between target object representations and global geometric features to predict object translation, rotation, and scale. Training progressively learns geometry-language alignment, introduces layout reasoning while preserving reconstruction capability, and refines physical consistency through collision-aware optimization. By separating spatial layout reasoning from asset synthesis, Fysiverse-3D-Vision provides an adaptable interface for interactive scene editing, object-level manipulations, and executable 3D content generation. Experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves superior geometric consistency, layout estimation, rendering quality, and physical property understanding compared with existing approaches.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: PhyVisGen: Physically and Visually High-Fidelity Robotic Manipulation Data Generation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yu Zheng, Qiyu Feng, Yixin Wu, Baoquan Yang, Yixuan Zhou
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: PhyVisGen is a high-fidelity framework for generating scalable robotic manipulation data, achieving 65-95% success in real tasks using solely synthetic demonstrations.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Large-scale manipulation demonstrations are essential for learning robust visuomotor policies, yet real-world data collection is expensive and difficult to scale. Simulation offers a promising alternative, but physical and visual discrepancies can limit the transferability of synthetic data, particularly for manipulation with soft grippers. We present PhyVisGen, a physically and visually high-fidelity framework for scalable robotic manipulation data generation. On the physical side, PhyVisGen introduces an arm-gripper coupling method based on the Incremental Potential Contact (IPC), enabling high-fidelity soft contact throughout complete manipulation trajectories. On the visual side, it combines real-scene reconstruction with real-time path tracing to generate visually realistic observations while preserving captured scene appearance. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate the physical and visual fidelity of PhyVisGen. Policies trained exclusively on synthetic manipulation demonstrations achieve 65-95% success across five real-robot tasks, without real-robot demonstration data or policy fine-tuning.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: DIFTA-3D: Depth-Consistent Instance-Level Feature Transfer and Adaptation of DINOv3 for 3D Detection
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Linman Wang, ZiFei Zhang, Chunran Zheng, Xiwang Dong, Jiarong Lin
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The paper presents DIFTA-3D, which enhances 3D instance detection by adapting DINOv3 for depth-consistent feature transfer, achieving improved mAP scores on ScanNetV2.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: RGB-D 3D instance detectors benefit from visual semantics, but the task-specific Faster R-CNN/ResNet branch used by IIFNet3D couples feature extraction to a separately trained 2D detector and its image-domain labels. In this work, we investigate this replacement through an adaptation of DINOv3 to the instance-level fusion pipeline of IIFNet3D. At the core of our approach is a depth-consistent feature pipeline that projects scene points into calibrated RGB-D frames, applies a metric depth-residual check, averages the accepted DINOv3 features into an offline point cache, and aggregates the cached features inside proposal-aligned RoI grids. On ScanNetV2, our DINOv3 control achieves mAP scores of 76.15 and 60.93 at IoU thresholds of 0.25 and 0.50, respectively. The Conservative VAID setting achieves mAP scores of 76.59 and 62.16, corresponding to numerical gains of 0.44 and 1.23 points over the control, respectively, in this checkpoint-level recipe comparison. The reported IIFNet3D result of 75.7/63.8 is used only as an external reference because the visual branch and processing protocol differ. Accordingly, we interpret these results as evidence for a controlled transfer recipe rather than as a causal estimate of the individual contributions of VAID or depth filtering.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: HazardArena: Evaluating Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Zixing Chen, Yifeng Gao, Li Wang, Yunhan Zhao, Yi Liu
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: HazardArena is a benchmark that evaluates semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action models, revealing vulnerabilities in action execution linked to contextual semantics and proposing a Safety Option Layer to mitigate risks.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich world knowledge from vision-language backbones and acquire executable skills via action demonstrations. However, existing evaluations largely focus on action execution success, leaving action policies loosely coupled with visual-linguistic semantics. This decoupling exposes a systematic vulnerability whereby correct action execution may induce unsafe outcomes under semantic risk. To expose this vulnerability, we introduce HazardArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate semantic safety in VLAs under controlled yet risk-bearing contexts. HazardArena is constructed from safe/unsafe twin scenarios that share matched objects, layouts, and action requirements, differing only in the semantic context that determines whether an action is unsafe. We find that VLA models trained exclusively on safe scenarios often fail to behave safely when evaluated in their corresponding unsafe counterparts. HazardArena includes over 2,000 assets and 40 risk-sensitive tasks spanning 7 real-world risk categories grounded in established robotic safety standards. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose a training-free Safety Option Layer that constrains action execution using semantic attributes or a vision-language judge, substantially reducing unsafe behaviors with minimal impact on task performance. We hope that HazardArena highlights the need to rethink how semantic safety is evaluated and enforced in VLAs as they scale toward real-world deployment. Code released at https://github.com/HazardArena-Team/HazardArena ; updated code availability information.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Fisheye-VLA: Decoupling Coverage and Acuity for Manipulation with a Single Fisheye Camera
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Ziang Ren, Zike Yan, Raymond Zhang, Xuguo He, Zhongyu Li
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Fisheye-VLA combines broad scene awareness and detailed feedback using a single fisheye camera, optimizing local visual focus for effective manipulation tasks.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Manipulation requires both broad scene awareness and detailed local feedback, yet conventional camera rigs provide them through separate front and wrist cameras. We present Fisheye-VLA, a visual interface that brings these capabilities together using a single passive fisheye. A global view preserves the workspace, while local perspective crops direct detail toward the interaction. The key design question is where this local visual budget should go. We answer it through a controlled re-rendering study, comparing alternative crop directions on the same recorded observations. The study finds that end-effector-centered views capture most of the estimated benefit of a much larger candidate pool, motivating a compact allocation around both hands. Our interface uses calibrated end-effector projection and motion lead to track the crops, while a shared ray encoding preserves their spatial meaning as they move. Integrated with a pretrained VLA, it achieves 84% and 82% success in the two expanded tabletop regions, where some target placements extend beyond the front-camera coverage, and supports shelf and conveyor manipulation. Ablations show that local crops and their viewing directions become more important in the larger workspace regions. The results demonstrate that a single fisheye can support these manipulation tasks without physical wrist cameras.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Robust Active-Perception Control for Global-State-Free Aerial-Ground Cooperation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiajun Yu, Baozhe Zhang, Pengxiang Zhou, Wentao Liu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The COPA framework enables robust aerial-ground cooperation by using a gimbal-mounted camera and TCN-based predictions to maintain target visibility without global localization.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Aerial-ground cooperation requires real-time UAV--UGV relative-state information. Instead of maintaining global estimates for both robots, direct control in a UGV-attached non-inertial frame avoids reliance on global localization. Vision-based relative pose estimation with a passive marker offers a low-cost and effective solution. However, a fixed camera may lose sight of the moving UGV when the required UAV attitude conflicts with the field-of-view (FOV) constraint. To address this, we propose COPA, a robust active-perception framework for global-state-free aerial-ground cooperation. We use a single-axis gimbal to decouple the camera optical axis from the UAV pitch attitude. We derive an active-perception model that relates UAV motion, gimbal angle, and UGV motion to the target image-plane state.A Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) predicts short-horizon UGV acceleration and angular velocity from recent motion history without global-state measurements. The model predictive control (MPC) uses these predictions to jointly optimize UAV and gimbal control. Simulations show that COPA maintains continuous target visibility, while ablation studies confirm that the TCN reduces peak errors during UGV motion transitions. Real-world experiments with UGV accelerations up to 3m/s^2 and yaw rates up to 1.0rad/s demonstrate robust tracking.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Fysiverse-3D-Vision Technical Report: Generating Executable 3D Worlds from Images through Unified Spatial Reasoning
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Dingkang Yang, Yizhou Liu, Wendong Cheng, Zizhi Chen, Shunli Wang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: Fysiverse-3D-Vision introduces a unified framework for generating executable 3D scenes from images, enhancing spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction for interactive content creation.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Generative models have advanced image-conditioned 3D content creation, yet generating controllable and executable 3D scenes from a single image remains challenging. Existing 3D generative approaches can synthesize visually plausible objects and scenes, but their spatial layout estimation is coupled with specific asset generators. They struggle to jointly model object semantics, metric geometry, and scene-level spatial relationships, which are essential for interactive editing, physical simulation, and embodied applications. We propose Fysiverse-3D-Vision, a unified vision-language-geometry framework for generative 3D scene reconstruction and executable asset construction from a single image. We establish a shared representation where spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction mutually enhance each other, allowing object layouts to be inferred beyond the constraints of individual asset generators. Our model integrates textual supervision, semantic visual cues, and geometric representations within a unified Transformer to capture scene context, metric geometry, and object-level interactions. An object-conditioned layout module performs cross-attention between target object representations and global geometric features to predict object translation, rotation, and scale. Training progressively learns geometry-language alignment, introduces layout reasoning while preserving reconstruction capability, and refines physical consistency through collision-aware optimization. By separating spatial layout reasoning from asset synthesis, Fysiverse-3D-Vision provides an adaptable interface for interactive scene editing, object-level manipulations, and executable 3D content generation. Experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves superior geometric consistency, layout estimation, rendering quality, and physical property understanding compared with existing approaches.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by predicting future interactions and actions using affordance-aware representations from diverse human videos.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: SurgMotion: A Video-Native Foundation Model for Universal Understanding of Surgical Videos
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Jinlin Wu, Felix Holm, Chuxi Chen, An Wang, Yaxin Hu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: SurgMotion is a video-native foundation model that enhances surgical video analysis by focusing on latent motion prediction, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: While foundation models have advanced surgical video analysis, current approaches rely predominantly on pixel-level reconstruction objectives that waste model capacity on low-level visual details, such as smoke, specular reflections, and fluid motion, rather than semantic structures essential for surgical understanding. We present SurgMotion, a video-native foundation model that shifts the learning paradigm from pixel-level reconstruction to latent motion prediction. Built on the Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA), SurgMotion introduces three key technical innovations tailored to surgical videos: (1) motion-guided latent masked prediction to prioritize semantically meaningful regions, (2) spatiotemporal affinity self-distillation to enforce relational consistency, and (3) spatiotemporal feature diversity regularization (SFDR) to prevent representation collapse in texture-sparse surgical scenes. To enable large-scale pretraining, we curate SurgMotion-15M, the largest surgical video dataset to date, comprising 3,658 hours of video from 50 sources across 13 anatomical regions. Extensive experiments across 17 benchmarks demonstrate that SurgMotion significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on surgical workflow recognition, achieving 14.6 percent improvement in F1 score on EgoSurgery and 10.3 percent on PitVis; on action triplet recognition with 39.54 percent mAP-IVT on CholecT50; as well as on skill assessment, polyp segmentation, and depth estimation. These results establish SurgMotion as a new standard for universal, motion-oriented surgical video understanding.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Spatiotemporal Calibration of Doppler Velocity Logs for Underwater Robots
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Hongxu Zhao, Guangyang Zeng, Yunling Shao, Tengfei Zhang, Junfeng Wu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper presents a Unified Iterative Calibration framework for Doppler Velocity Logs, enhancing underwater SLAM accuracy by jointly estimating extrinsic parameters and time offsets using Gaussian Process motion priors.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: The calibration of extrinsic parameters and clock offsets between sensors for high-accuracy performance in underwater SLAM systems remains insufficiently explored. Existing methods for Doppler Velocity Log (DVL) calibration are either constrained to specific sensor configurations or rely on oversimplified assumptions, and none jointly estimate translational extrinsics and time offsets. We propose a Unified Iterative Calibration (UIC) framework for general DVL sensor setups, formulated as a Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation with a Gaussian Process (GP) motion prior for high-fidelity motion interpolation. UIC alternates between efficient GP-based motion state updates and gradient-based calibration variable updates, supported by a provably statistically consistent sequential initialization scheme. The proposed UIC can be applied to IMU, cameras and other modalities as co-sensors. We release an open-source DVL-camera calibration toolbox. Beyond underwater applications, several aspects of UIC-such as the integration of GP priors for MAP-based calibration and the design of provably reliable initialization procedures-are broadly applicable to other multi-sensor calibration problems. Finally, simulations and real-world tests validate our approach.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: EndoCogniAgent: Closed-Loop Agentic Reasoning with Self-Consistency Validation for Endoscopic Diagnosis
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yi Tang, Kai-Ni Wang, Liang-Peng Pu, Hui Tang, Xiaopu He
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: EndoCogniAgent enhances endoscopic diagnosis by integrating visual and textual evidence through a closed-loop reasoning framework, achieving improved accuracy and diagnostic quality.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Endoscopic diagnosis is an iterative process in which clinicians acquire, compare, and verify local visual evidence before reaching a conclusion. Current AI systems do not adequately support this process because fine-grained evidence acquisition and multi-step reasoning remain weakly coupled, complicating reconciliation of image-derived findings with their textual interpretations. This gives rise to two failure modes, hallucinated evidence and uncorrected error accumulation, that undermine diagnostic reliability. We propose EndoCogniAgent, a closed-loop agentic framework that formulates endoscopic diagnosis as a controlled state update process for integrating complementary visual and textual evidence. At each reasoning round, a central planner selects an evidence acquisition action, specialized expert tools extract spatial and semantic observations as structured textual evidence, and a self-consistency validation mechanism examines this evidence along two dimensions, knowledge consistency against the input image and temporal consistency with prior validated findings, before updating the diagnostic state. Validated observations are admitted into the evolving state to condition subsequent planning, while insufficiently supported or conflicting findings are retained with corrective feedback that redirects the planner toward additional verification. We further introduce EndoAgentBench, a workflow-oriented benchmark comprising 6,132 question-answer pairs from 11 endoscopic datasets, to evaluate diagnostic agents across a comprehensive diagnostic chain, from fine-grained visual perception to high-level diagnostic reasoning. EndoCogniAgent achieves 85.23% overall accuracy on perception tasks and 71.13% clinical acceptance rate on reasoning tasks. Blinded clinician evaluation further shows consistent improvements in diagnostic response quality over the evaluated baselines.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Whole-Body UMI: Transferring UMI Manipulation Skills to Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation via Real-Time Motion Generation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yuxuan Nai, Leixin Chang, Liangjing Yang, Shuo Yang, Zhongyu Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The Whole-Body UMI (WB-UMI) enables real-time, scalable humanoid manipulation by decoupling coordination from task semantics, achieving high success rates across multiple tasks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Collecting whole-body demonstrations for humanoid manipulation mostly relies on teleoperation, which is costly and hard to scale up. The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) provides a scalable data collection paradigm, but end-effector trajectories alone underdetermine humanoid whole-body coordination, which is insufficient for whole-body demonstration collection. Therefore, we introduce Whole-Body UMI (WB-UMI), a task-agnostic, real-time and end-effector conditioned motion generator that decouples whole-body coordination learning from task semantics learning through a shared end-effector interface. A diffusion policy learns from native UMI demonstrations, while WB-UMI learns independently from retargeted motion capture, requiring no body trackers or paired image--whole-body demonstrations during task-specific data collection. In real deployment, an asynchronous hierarchy integrates the diffusion policy, motion generator, and a whole-body controller with latency compensation and measured-state feedback. Real-robot experiments on G1 support real-time closed-loop transfer across four tasks, achieving 90% success in drawer closing, 80% in shelf pick-and-place, 30% in ball toss, and 40% in Loco-PnP, which shows the effectiveness of this hierarchy in transferring native UMI skills to humanoid whole-body manipulation.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Fisheye-VLA: Decoupling Coverage and Acuity for Manipulation with a Single Fisheye Camera
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Ziang Ren, Zike Yan, Raymond Zhang, Xuguo He, Zhongyu Li
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: Fisheye-VLA combines broad scene awareness and detailed feedback using a single fisheye camera, optimizing local visual focus for effective manipulation tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Manipulation requires both broad scene awareness and detailed local feedback, yet conventional camera rigs provide them through separate front and wrist cameras. We present Fisheye-VLA, a visual interface that brings these capabilities together using a single passive fisheye. A global view preserves the workspace, while local perspective crops direct detail toward the interaction. The key design question is where this local visual budget should go. We answer it through a controlled re-rendering study, comparing alternative crop directions on the same recorded observations. The study finds that end-effector-centered views capture most of the estimated benefit of a much larger candidate pool, motivating a compact allocation around both hands. Our interface uses calibrated end-effector projection and motion lead to track the crops, while a shared ray encoding preserves their spatial meaning as they move. Integrated with a pretrained VLA, it achieves 84% and 82% success in the two expanded tabletop regions, where some target placements extend beyond the front-camera coverage, and supports shelf and conveyor manipulation. Ablations show that local crops and their viewing directions become more important in the larger workspace regions. The results demonstrate that a single fisheye can support these manipulation tasks without physical wrist cameras.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Robust Active-Perception Control for Global-State-Free Aerial-Ground Cooperation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiajun Yu, Baozhe Zhang, Pengxiang Zhou, Wentao Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The COPA framework enables robust aerial-ground cooperation by using a gimbal-mounted camera and TCN-based predictions to maintain target visibility without global localization.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Aerial-ground cooperation requires real-time UAV--UGV relative-state information. Instead of maintaining global estimates for both robots, direct control in a UGV-attached non-inertial frame avoids reliance on global localization. Vision-based relative pose estimation with a passive marker offers a low-cost and effective solution. However, a fixed camera may lose sight of the moving UGV when the required UAV attitude conflicts with the field-of-view (FOV) constraint. To address this, we propose COPA, a robust active-perception framework for global-state-free aerial-ground cooperation. We use a single-axis gimbal to decouple the camera optical axis from the UAV pitch attitude. We derive an active-perception model that relates UAV motion, gimbal angle, and UGV motion to the target image-plane state.A Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) predicts short-horizon UGV acceleration and angular velocity from recent motion history without global-state measurements. The model predictive control (MPC) uses these predictions to jointly optimize UAV and gimbal control. Simulations show that COPA maintains continuous target visibility, while ablation studies confirm that the TCN reduces peak errors during UGV motion transitions. Real-world experiments with UGV accelerations up to 3m/s^2 and yaw rates up to 1.0rad/s demonstrate robust tracking.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Mira-Scene: Pixel-Aligned Layouts for Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yang-Tian Sun, Tianjia Liu, Zehuan Huang, Yi-Hua Huang, Xiaoyang Lyu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Mira-Scene introduces a novel compositional framework for 3D scene reconstruction that enhances layout accuracy by utilizing pixel-aligned mappings and multimodal diffusion transformers.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Single-image 3D object generation can now produce high-fidelity assets, yet accurately placing them into a coherent scene layout remains an open challenge. A central difficulty lies in how object layout is represented. Holistic methods absorb placement into a scene-level generation process, sacrificing object-level detail. Compositional methods preserve object fidelity by decoupling geometry from layout, but typically parameterize layout as sparse, unbounded pose variables that are difficult to learn and generalize poorly under scarce scene-level supervision. We present Mira-Scene, a compositional 3D scene reconstruction framework that replaces sparse pose regression with dense, bounded correspondence recovery. At its core is the Canonical Coordinate Map (CCM), a pixel-aligned field that maps each visible object pixel to a surface coordinate in the object's bounded canonical space. When paired with a scene-space Point Cloud Map (PCM) from monocular geometry estimation, CCM induces dense canonical-to-scene correspondences from which object transformations are recovered through robust geometric alignment. Because CCM operates in bounded canonical space, it provides a stable prediction target that can be trained from scalable object-level 3D data without requiring scene-level layout annotations. Mira-Scene further introduces a multimodal diffusion transformer that jointly generates object geometry and CCMs, using modality-specific expert streams with shared attention and positional encoding to promote geometry-layout consistency. Experiments on indoor, outdoor, synthetic, and in-the-wild scenes show that Mira-Scene substantially outperforms strong baselines in layout accuracy, achieving relative gains of 39.8% in 3D-IoU and 16.5% in 2D-IoU over SAM3D, using limited open-source training data.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: The Tasteful Agent: Measuring and Improving Taste in Long-Horizon Tasks
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Wenbo Pan, Zhichao Liu, Shujie Liu, Jingying Zeng, Chin-Yew Lin
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper introduces Taste-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate and enhance the decision-making "taste" of LLM agents in long-horizon tasks, revealing significant challenges and training potential.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: LLM agents increasingly work on long-horizon tasks, and the decisions they make along the way, such as which hypothesis to test or which implementation to build on, determine the outcome of the whole run. Making these decisions well is becoming a key capability for both engineering and research agents. We refer to the ability to make good long-horizon decisions as the taste of an agent. While existing benchmarks measure the end-to-end success of agents on long-horizon tasks, none of them measures the taste of an agent. To address this problem, we build Taste-Bench, a benchmark of taste questions constructed automatically from trajectories that agents produced in engineering and research tasks. Each question presents a decision fork, a point in a trajectory where multiple directions are available and one of them leads to a better outcome, and the evaluated model chooses among these directions without seeing what happens after the fork. We mine these forks automatically from parallel attempts at the same task and from detours inside a single trajectory, without needing human annotation. We evaluate frontier models on Taste-Bench and find that the best model answers only 59.7% of the questions correctly. We further find that forks whose deciding evidence appears later in the trajectory are much harder for every model, and that a larger reasoning budget does not improve the accuracy. Finally, we show that taste can be trained. We distill the judgment of a teacher that has seen the outcome into a student model, and the student makes better decisions on unseen tasks and improves end-to-end success on held-out SWE-bench Pro tasks.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: LiFR v2: Completion-Augmented Event Propagation for High-Rate Dense Prediction
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Tao Wan, Xiaoshan Wu, Yifei Yu, Bo Wang, Xiaoyang Lyu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: LiFR v2 enhances high-rate dense prediction by integrating RGB keyframes and event data through a novel framework, achieving superior performance in semantic segmentation and depth estimation.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: High-rate dense perception in dynamic environments is limited by the low update rate of RGB cameras, as rapid scene changes can occur between frames. Event cameras offer temporally dense but spatially sparse measurements, complementary to spatially dense RGB observations. Direct fusion cannot fully exploit this complementarity, while event-guided propagation fails on newly appearing or disoccluded regions without valid RGB support. We present LiFR v2, a unified propagation-completion-memory framework for causal anytime and streaming dense prediction from an RGB keyframe and events. LiFR v2 introduces an Event-Guided Completion Module (EGCM) to recover task-relevant representations where propagation is unsupported, and a History Retrieval Module (HRM) to reuse completed representations across successive queries. The framework supports semantic segmentation, monocular depth estimation, and multi-task dense prediction, and we further introduce SHF-Emerge to evaluate rapid object emergence and disocclusion. LiFR v2 achieves 74.37% mIoU on DSEC and 56.13% on SHF-Emerge, improving LiFR-Seg by 1.85 percentage points on the latter, while reducing SHF-Emerge depth RMSE from 1.564 m to 1.118 m over the propagation baseline. It also exceeds 100 FPS for both segmentation and depth, demonstrating accurate and efficient high-rate perception beyond RGB frame rates.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Fysiverse-3D-Vision Technical Report: Generating Executable 3D Worlds from Images through Unified Spatial Reasoning
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Dingkang Yang, Yizhou Liu, Wendong Cheng, Zizhi Chen, Shunli Wang
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: Fysiverse-3D-Vision introduces a unified framework for generating executable 3D scenes from images, enhancing spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction for interactive content creation.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Generative models have advanced image-conditioned 3D content creation, yet generating controllable and executable 3D scenes from a single image remains challenging. Existing 3D generative approaches can synthesize visually plausible objects and scenes, but their spatial layout estimation is coupled with specific asset generators. They struggle to jointly model object semantics, metric geometry, and scene-level spatial relationships, which are essential for interactive editing, physical simulation, and embodied applications. We propose Fysiverse-3D-Vision, a unified vision-language-geometry framework for generative 3D scene reconstruction and executable asset construction from a single image. We establish a shared representation where spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction mutually enhance each other, allowing object layouts to be inferred beyond the constraints of individual asset generators. Our model integrates textual supervision, semantic visual cues, and geometric representations within a unified Transformer to capture scene context, metric geometry, and object-level interactions. An object-conditioned layout module performs cross-attention between target object representations and global geometric features to predict object translation, rotation, and scale. Training progressively learns geometry-language alignment, introduces layout reasoning while preserving reconstruction capability, and refines physical consistency through collision-aware optimization. By separating spatial layout reasoning from asset synthesis, Fysiverse-3D-Vision provides an adaptable interface for interactive scene editing, object-level manipulations, and executable 3D content generation. Experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves superior geometric consistency, layout estimation, rendering quality, and physical property understanding compared with existing approaches.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: PhyVisGen: Physically and Visually High-Fidelity Robotic Manipulation Data Generation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yu Zheng, Qiyu Feng, Yixin Wu, Baoquan Yang, Yixuan Zhou
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: PhyVisGen is a high-fidelity framework for generating scalable robotic manipulation data, achieving 65-95% success in real tasks using solely synthetic demonstrations.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Large-scale manipulation demonstrations are essential for learning robust visuomotor policies, yet real-world data collection is expensive and difficult to scale. Simulation offers a promising alternative, but physical and visual discrepancies can limit the transferability of synthetic data, particularly for manipulation with soft grippers. We present PhyVisGen, a physically and visually high-fidelity framework for scalable robotic manipulation data generation. On the physical side, PhyVisGen introduces an arm-gripper coupling method based on the Incremental Potential Contact (IPC), enabling high-fidelity soft contact throughout complete manipulation trajectories. On the visual side, it combines real-scene reconstruction with real-time path tracing to generate visually realistic observations while preserving captured scene appearance. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate the physical and visual fidelity of PhyVisGen. Policies trained exclusively on synthetic manipulation demonstrations achieve 65-95% success across five real-robot tasks, without real-robot demonstration data or policy fine-tuning.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by predicting future interactions and actions using affordance-aware representations from diverse human videos.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: SurgMotion: A Video-Native Foundation Model for Universal Understanding of Surgical Videos
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Jinlin Wu, Felix Holm, Chuxi Chen, An Wang, Yaxin Hu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: SurgMotion is a video-native foundation model that enhances surgical video analysis by focusing on latent motion prediction, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: While foundation models have advanced surgical video analysis, current approaches rely predominantly on pixel-level reconstruction objectives that waste model capacity on low-level visual details, such as smoke, specular reflections, and fluid motion, rather than semantic structures essential for surgical understanding. We present SurgMotion, a video-native foundation model that shifts the learning paradigm from pixel-level reconstruction to latent motion prediction. Built on the Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA), SurgMotion introduces three key technical innovations tailored to surgical videos: (1) motion-guided latent masked prediction to prioritize semantically meaningful regions, (2) spatiotemporal affinity self-distillation to enforce relational consistency, and (3) spatiotemporal feature diversity regularization (SFDR) to prevent representation collapse in texture-sparse surgical scenes. To enable large-scale pretraining, we curate SurgMotion-15M, the largest surgical video dataset to date, comprising 3,658 hours of video from 50 sources across 13 anatomical regions. Extensive experiments across 17 benchmarks demonstrate that SurgMotion significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on surgical workflow recognition, achieving 14.6 percent improvement in F1 score on EgoSurgery and 10.3 percent on PitVis; on action triplet recognition with 39.54 percent mAP-IVT on CholecT50; as well as on skill assessment, polyp segmentation, and depth estimation. These results establish SurgMotion as a new standard for universal, motion-oriented surgical video understanding.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Spatiotemporal Calibration of Doppler Velocity Logs for Underwater Robots
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Hongxu Zhao, Guangyang Zeng, Yunling Shao, Tengfei Zhang, Junfeng Wu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents a Unified Iterative Calibration framework for Doppler Velocity Logs, enhancing underwater SLAM accuracy by jointly estimating extrinsic parameters and time offsets using Gaussian Process motion priors.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: The calibration of extrinsic parameters and clock offsets between sensors for high-accuracy performance in underwater SLAM systems remains insufficiently explored. Existing methods for Doppler Velocity Log (DVL) calibration are either constrained to specific sensor configurations or rely on oversimplified assumptions, and none jointly estimate translational extrinsics and time offsets. We propose a Unified Iterative Calibration (UIC) framework for general DVL sensor setups, formulated as a Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation with a Gaussian Process (GP) motion prior for high-fidelity motion interpolation. UIC alternates between efficient GP-based motion state updates and gradient-based calibration variable updates, supported by a provably statistically consistent sequential initialization scheme. The proposed UIC can be applied to IMU, cameras and other modalities as co-sensors. We release an open-source DVL-camera calibration toolbox. Beyond underwater applications, several aspects of UIC-such as the integration of GP priors for MAP-based calibration and the design of provably reliable initialization procedures-are broadly applicable to other multi-sensor calibration problems. Finally, simulations and real-world tests validate our approach.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: EndoCogniAgent: Closed-Loop Agentic Reasoning with Self-Consistency Validation for Endoscopic Diagnosis
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yi Tang, Kai-Ni Wang, Liang-Peng Pu, Hui Tang, Xiaopu He
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: EndoCogniAgent enhances endoscopic diagnosis by integrating visual and textual evidence through a closed-loop reasoning framework, achieving improved accuracy and diagnostic quality.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Endoscopic diagnosis is an iterative process in which clinicians acquire, compare, and verify local visual evidence before reaching a conclusion. Current AI systems do not adequately support this process because fine-grained evidence acquisition and multi-step reasoning remain weakly coupled, complicating reconciliation of image-derived findings with their textual interpretations. This gives rise to two failure modes, hallucinated evidence and uncorrected error accumulation, that undermine diagnostic reliability. We propose EndoCogniAgent, a closed-loop agentic framework that formulates endoscopic diagnosis as a controlled state update process for integrating complementary visual and textual evidence. At each reasoning round, a central planner selects an evidence acquisition action, specialized expert tools extract spatial and semantic observations as structured textual evidence, and a self-consistency validation mechanism examines this evidence along two dimensions, knowledge consistency against the input image and temporal consistency with prior validated findings, before updating the diagnostic state. Validated observations are admitted into the evolving state to condition subsequent planning, while insufficiently supported or conflicting findings are retained with corrective feedback that redirects the planner toward additional verification. We further introduce EndoAgentBench, a workflow-oriented benchmark comprising 6,132 question-answer pairs from 11 endoscopic datasets, to evaluate diagnostic agents across a comprehensive diagnostic chain, from fine-grained visual perception to high-level diagnostic reasoning. EndoCogniAgent achieves 85.23% overall accuracy on perception tasks and 71.13% clinical acceptance rate on reasoning tasks. Blinded clinician evaluation further shows consistent improvements in diagnostic response quality over the evaluated baselines.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: DIFTA-3D: Depth-Consistent Instance-Level Feature Transfer and Adaptation of DINOv3 for 3D Detection
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Linman Wang, ZiFei Zhang, Chunran Zheng, Xiwang Dong, Jiarong Lin
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents DIFTA-3D, which enhances 3D instance detection by adapting DINOv3 for depth-consistent feature transfer, achieving improved mAP scores on ScanNetV2.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: RGB-D 3D instance detectors benefit from visual semantics, but the task-specific Faster R-CNN/ResNet branch used by IIFNet3D couples feature extraction to a separately trained 2D detector and its image-domain labels. Replacing that branch with a frozen vision foundation model removes this task-specific dependency, but may introduce occlusion noise and a mismatch between patch features and geometry-aware detection features. In this work, we investigate this replacement through an adaptation of DINOv3 to the instance-level fusion pipeline of IIFNet3D. At the core of our approach is a depth-consistent feature pipeline that projects scene points into calibrated RGB-D frames, applies a metric depth-residual check, averages the accepted DINOv3 features into an offline point cache, and aggregates the cached features inside proposal-aligned RoI grids. The geometric and bidirectional instance-fusion paths are preserved, while Conservative VAID is evaluated as a low-strength, support-weighted semantic distillation recipe applied only to positive RoIs. We conduct extensive evaluations on ScanNetV2 to assess the proposed transfer recipes. On ScanNetV2, our DINOv3 control achieves mAP scores of 76.15 and 60.93 at IoU thresholds of 0.25 and 0.50, respectively. The Conservative VAID setting achieves mAP scores of 76.59 and 62.16, corresponding to numerical gains of 0.44 and 1.23 points over the control, respectively, in this checkpoint-level recipe comparison. The reported IIFNet3D result of 75.7/63.8 is used only as an external reference because the visual branch and processing protocol differ. Accordingly, we interpret these results as evidence for a controlled transfer recipe rather than as a causal estimate of the individual contributions of VAID or depth filtering.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: Whole-Body UMI: Transferring UMI Manipulation Skills to Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation via Real-Time Motion Generation
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Yuxuan Nai, Leixin Chang, Liangjing Yang, Shuo Yang, Zhongyu Li
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: The Whole-Body UMI (WB-UMI) enables real-time, scalable humanoid manipulation by decoupling coordination from task semantics, achieving high success rates across multiple tasks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Collecting whole-body demonstrations for humanoid manipulation mostly relies on teleoperation, which is costly and hard to scale up. The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) provides a scalable data collection paradigm, but end-effector trajectories alone underdetermine humanoid whole-body coordination, which is insufficient for whole-body demonstration collection. Therefore, we introduce Whole-Body UMI (WB-UMI), a task-agnostic, real-time and end-effector conditioned motion generator that decouples whole-body coordination learning from task semantics learning through a shared end-effector interface. A diffusion policy learns from native UMI demonstrations, while WB-UMI learns independently from retargeted motion capture, requiring no body trackers or paired image--whole-body demonstrations during task-specific data collection. In real deployment, an asynchronous hierarchy integrates the diffusion policy, motion generator, and a whole-body controller with latency compensation and measured-state feedback. Real-robot experiments on G1 support real-time closed-loop transfer across four tasks, achieving 90% success in drawer closing, 80% in shelf pick-and-place, 30% in ball toss, and 40% in Loco-PnP, which shows the effectiveness of this hierarchy in transferring native UMI skills to humanoid whole-body manipulation.

香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.title: HazardArena: Evaluating Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.authors_text: Zixing Chen, Yifeng Gao, Li Wang, Yunhan Zhao, Yi Liu
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.summary: HazardArena is a benchmark that evaluates semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action models, revealing vulnerabilities in action execution linked to contextual semantics and proposing a Safety Option Layer to mitigate risks.
香港大学机械工程系机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich world knowledge from vision-language backbones and acquire executable skills via action demonstrations. However, existing evaluations largely focus on action execution success, leaving action policies loosely coupled with visual-linguistic semantics. This decoupling exposes a systematic vulnerability whereby correct action execution may induce unsafe outcomes under semantic risk. To expose this vulnerability, we introduce HazardArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate semantic safety in VLAs under controlled yet risk-bearing contexts. HazardArena is constructed from safe/unsafe twin scenarios that share matched objects, layouts, and action requirements, differing only in the semantic context that determines whether an action is unsafe. We find that VLA models trained exclusively on safe scenarios often fail to behave safely when evaluated in their corresponding unsafe counterparts. HazardArena includes over 2,000 assets and 40 risk-sensitive tasks spanning 7 real-world risk categories grounded in established robotic safety standards. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose a training-free Safety Option Layer that constrains action execution using semantic attributes or a vision-language judge, substantially reducing unsafe behaviors with minimal impact on task performance. We hope that HazardArena highlights the need to rethink how semantic safety is evaluated and enforced in VLAs as they scale toward real-world deployment. Code released at https://github.com/HazardArena-Team/HazardArena ; updated code availability information.

机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Wenbo Pan, Zhichao Liu, Shujie Liu, Jingying Zeng, Chin-Yew Lin
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper introduces Taste-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate and enhance the decision-making "taste" of LLM agents in long-horizon tasks, revealing significant challenges and training potential.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: LLM agents increasingly work on long-horizon tasks, and the decisions they make along the way, such as which hypothesis to test or which implementation to build on, determine the outcome of the whole run. Making these decisions well is becoming a key capability for both engineering and research agents. We refer to the ability to make good long-horizon decisions as the taste of an agent. While existing benchmarks measure the end-to-end success of agents on long-horizon tasks, none of them measures the taste of an agent. We mine these forks automatically from parallel attempts at the same task and from detours inside a single trajectory, without needing human annotation. We evaluate frontier models on Taste-Bench and find that the best model answers only 59.7% of the questions correctly. We further find that forks whose deciding evidence appears later in the trajectory are much harder for every model, and that a larger reasoning budget does not improve the accuracy. Finally, we show that taste can be trained. We distill the judgment of a teacher that has seen the outcome into a student model, and the student makes better decisions on unseen tasks and improves end-to-end success on held-out SWE-bench Pro tasks.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Fysiverse-3D-Vision Technical Report: Generating Executable 3D Worlds from Images through Unified Spatial Reasoning
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Dingkang Yang, Yizhou Liu, Wendong Cheng, Zizhi Chen, Shunli Wang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: Fysiverse-3D-Vision introduces a unified framework for generating executable 3D scenes from images, enhancing spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction for interactive content creation.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Generative models have advanced image-conditioned 3D content creation, yet generating controllable and executable 3D scenes from a single image remains challenging. We establish a shared representation where spatial reasoning and geometric reconstruction mutually enhance each other, allowing object layouts to be inferred beyond the constraints of individual asset generators. Our model integrates textual supervision, semantic visual cues, and geometric representations within a unified Transformer to capture scene context, metric geometry, and object-level interactions. An object-conditioned layout module performs cross-attention between target object representations and global geometric features to predict object translation, rotation, and scale. 机器人与自动化研究中心.title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by predicting future interactions and actions using affordance-aware representations from diverse human videos.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: SurgMotion: A Video-Native Foundation Model for Universal Understanding of Surgical Videos
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Jinlin Wu, Felix Holm, Chuxi Chen, An Wang, Yaxin Hu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: SurgMotion is a video-native foundation model that enhances surgical video analysis by focusing on latent motion prediction, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: While foundation models have advanced surgical video analysis, current approaches rely predominantly on pixel-level reconstruction objectives that waste model capacity on low-level visual details, such as smoke, specular reflections, and fluid motion, rather than semantic structures essential for surgical understanding. These results establish SurgMotion as a new standard for universal, motion-oriented surgical video understanding.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Spatiotemporal Calibration of Doppler Velocity Logs for Underwater Robots
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Hongxu Zhao, Guangyang Zeng, Yunling Shao, Tengfei Zhang, Junfeng Wu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper presents a Unified Iterative Calibration framework for Doppler Velocity Logs, enhancing underwater SLAM accuracy by jointly estimating extrinsic parameters and time offsets using Gaussian Process motion priors.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: The calibration of extrinsic parameters and clock offsets between sensors for high-accuracy performance in underwater SLAM systems remains insufficiently explored. Existing methods for Doppler Velocity Log (DVL) calibration are either constrained to specific sensor configurations or rely on oversimplified assumptions, and none jointly estimate translational extrinsics and time offsets. We propose a Unified Iterative Calibration (UIC) framework for general DVL sensor setups, formulated as a Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation with a Gaussian Process (GP) motion prior for high-fidelity motion interpolation. UIC alternates between efficient GP-based motion state updates and gradient-based calibration variable updates, supported by a provably statistically consistent sequential initialization scheme. The proposed UIC can be applied to IMU, cameras and other modalities as co-sensors. We release an open-source DVL-camera calibration toolbox. Beyond underwater applications, several aspects of UIC-such as the integration of GP priors for MAP-based calibration and the design of provably reliable initialization procedures-are broadly applicable to other multi-sensor calibration problems. Finally, simulations and real-world tests validate our approach.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: EndoCogniAgent: Closed-Loop Agentic Reasoning with Self-Consistency Validation for Endoscopic Diagnosis
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yi Tang, Kai-Ni Wang, Liang-Peng Pu, Hui Tang, Xiaopu He
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: EndoCogniAgent enhances endoscopic diagnosis by integrating visual and textual evidence through a closed-loop reasoning framework, achieving improved accuracy and diagnostic quality.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Endoscopic diagnosis is an iterative process in which clinicians acquire, compare, and verify local visual evidence before reaching a conclusion. Current AI systems do not adequately support this process because fine-grained evidence acquisition and multi-step reasoning remain weakly coupled, complicating reconciliation of image-derived findings with their textual interpretations. This gives rise to two failure modes, hallucinated evidence and uncorrected error accumulation, that undermine diagnostic reliability. We propose EndoCogniAgent, a closed-loop agentic framework that formulates endoscopic diagnosis as a controlled state update process for integrating complementary visual and textual evidence. At each reasoning round, a central planner selects an evidence acquisition action, specialized expert tools extract spatial and semantic observations as structured textual evidence, and a self-consistency validation mechanism examines this evidence along two dimensions, knowledge consistency against the input image and temporal consistency with prior validated findings, before updating the diagnostic state. Validated observations are admitted into the evolving state to condition subsequent planning, while insufficiently supported or conflicting findings are retained with corrective feedback that redirects the planner toward additional verification. We further introduce EndoAgentBench, a workflow-oriented benchmark comprising 6,132 question-answer pairs from 11 endoscopic datasets, to evaluate diagnostic agents across a comprehensive diagnostic chain, from fine-grained visual perception to high-level diagnostic reasoning. EndoCogniAgent achieves 85.23% overall accuracy on perception tasks and 71.13% clinical acceptance rate on reasoning tasks. Blinded clinician evaluation further shows consistent improvements in diagnostic response quality over the evaluated baselines.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Whole-Body UMI: Transferring UMI Manipulation Skills to Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation via Real-Time Motion Generation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yuxuan Nai, Leixin Chang, Liangjing Yang, Shuo Yang, Zhongyu Li
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The Whole-Body UMI (WB-UMI) enables real-time, scalable humanoid manipulation by decoupling coordination from task semantics, achieving high success rates across multiple tasks.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Collecting whole-body demonstrations for humanoid manipulation mostly relies on teleoperation, which is costly and hard to scale up. The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) provides a scalable data collection paradigm, but end-effector trajectories alone underdetermine humanoid whole-body coordination, which is insufficient for whole-body demonstration collection. Therefore, we introduce Whole-Body UMI (WB-UMI), a task-agnostic, real-time and end-effector conditioned motion generator that decouples whole-body coordination learning from task semantics learning through a shared end-effector interface. A diffusion policy learns from native UMI demonstrations, while WB-UMI learns independently from retargeted motion capture, requiring no body trackers or paired image--whole-body demonstrations during task-specific data collection. In real deployment, an asynchronous hierarchy integrates the diffusion policy, motion generator, and a whole-body controller with latency compensation and measured-state feedback. Real-robot experiments on G1 support real-time closed-loop transfer across four tasks, achieving 90% success in drawer closing, 80% in shelf pick-and-place, 30% in ball toss, and 40% in Loco-PnP, which shows the effectiveness of this hierarchy in transferring native UMI skills to humanoid whole-body manipulation.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: HazardArena: Evaluating Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Zixing Chen, Yifeng Gao, Li Wang, Yunhan Zhao, Yi Liu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: HazardArena is a benchmark that evaluates semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action models, revealing vulnerabilities in action execution linked to contextual semantics and proposing a Safety Option Layer to mitigate risks.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich world knowledge from vision-language backbones and acquire executable skills via action demonstrations. However, existing evaluations largely focus on action execution success, leaving action policies loosely coupled with visual-linguistic semantics. This decoupling exposes a systematic vulnerability whereby correct action execution may induce unsafe outcomes under semantic risk. To expose this vulnerability, we introduce HazardArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate semantic safety in VLAs under controlled yet risk-bearing contexts. HazardArena is constructed from safe/unsafe twin scenarios that share matched objects, layouts, and action requirements, differing only in the semantic context that determines whether an action is unsafe. We find that VLA models trained exclusively on safe scenarios often fail to behave safely when evaluated in their corresponding unsafe counterparts. HazardArena includes over 2,000 assets and 40 risk-sensitive tasks spanning 7 real-world risk categories grounded in established robotic safety standards. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose a training-free Safety Option Layer that constrains action execution using semantic attributes or a vision-language judge, substantially reducing unsafe behaviors with minimal impact on task performance. We hope that HazardArena highlights the need to rethink how semantic safety is evaluated and enforced in VLAs as they scale toward real-world deployment. Code released at https://github.com/HazardArena-Team/HazardArena ; updated code availability information.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Fisheye-VLA: Decoupling Coverage and Acuity for Manipulation with a Single Fisheye Camera
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Ziang Ren, Zike Yan, Raymond Zhang, Xuguo He, Zhongyu Li
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: Fisheye-VLA combines broad scene awareness and detailed feedback using a single fisheye camera, optimizing local visual focus for effective manipulation tasks.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Manipulation requires both broad scene awareness and detailed local feedback, yet conventional camera rigs provide them through separate front and wrist cameras. We present Fisheye-VLA, a visual interface that brings these capabilities together using a single passive fisheye. A global view preserves the workspace, while local perspective crops direct detail toward the interaction. The key design question is where this local visual budget should go. We answer it through a controlled re-rendering study, comparing alternative crop directions on the same recorded observations. The study finds that end-effector-centered views capture most of the estimated benefit of a much larger candidate pool, motivating a compact allocation around both hands. Our interface uses calibrated end-effector projection and motion lead to track the crops, while a shared ray encoding preserves their spatial meaning as they move. Integrated with a pretrained VLA, it achieves 84% and 82% success in the two expanded tabletop regions, where some target placements extend beyond the front-camera coverage, and supports shelf and conveyor manipulation. Ablations show that local crops and their viewing directions become more important in the larger workspace regions. The results demonstrate that a single fisheye can support these manipulation tasks without physical wrist cameras.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Robust Active-Perception Control for Global-State-Free Aerial-Ground Cooperation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiajun Yu, Baozhe Zhang, Pengxiang Zhou, Wentao Liu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The COPA framework enables robust aerial-ground cooperation by using a gimbal-mounted camera and TCN-based predictions to maintain target visibility without global localization.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Aerial-ground cooperation requires real-time UAV--UGV relative-state information. Instead of maintaining global estimates for both robots, direct control in a UGV-attached non-inertial frame avoids reliance on global localization. Vision-based relative pose estimation with a passive marker offers a low-cost and effective solution. However, a fixed camera may lose sight of the moving UGV when the required UAV attitude conflicts with the field-of-view (FOV) constraint. To address this, we propose COPA, a robust active-perception framework for global-state-free aerial-ground cooperation. We use a single-axis gimbal to decouple the camera optical axis from the UAV pitch attitude. We derive an active-perception model that relates UAV motion, gimbal angle, and UGV motion to the target image-plane state.A Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) predicts short-horizon UGV acceleration and angular velocity from recent motion history without global-state measurements. The model predictive control (MPC) uses these predictions to jointly optimize UAV and gimbal control. Simulations show that COPA maintains continuous target visibility, while ablation studies confirm that the TCN reduces peak errors during UGV motion transitions. Real-world experiments with UGV accelerations up to 3m/s^2 and yaw rates up to 1.0rad/s demonstrate robust tracking.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Mira-Scene: Pixel-Aligned Layouts for Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yang-Tian Sun, Tianjia Liu, Zehuan Huang, Yi-Hua Huang, Xiaoyang Lyu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: Mira-Scene introduces a novel compositional framework for 3D scene reconstruction that enhances layout accuracy by utilizing pixel-aligned mappings and multimodal diffusion transformers.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Single-image 3D object generation can now produce high-fidelity assets, yet accurately placing them into a coherent scene layout remains an open challenge. A central difficulty lies in how object layout is represented. Holistic methods absorb placement into a scene-level generation process, sacrificing object-level detail. Compositional methods preserve object fidelity by decoupling geometry from layout, but typically parameterize layout as sparse, unbounded pose variables that are difficult to learn and generalize poorly under scarce scene-level supervision. When paired with a scene-space Point Cloud Map (PCM) from monocular geometry estimation, CCM induces dense canonical-to-scene correspondences from which object transformations are recovered through robust geometric alignment. Because CCM operates in bounded canonical space, it provides a stable prediction target that can be trained from scalable object-level 3D data without requiring scene-level layout annotations. Mira-Scene further introduces a multimodal diffusion transformer that jointly generates object geometry and CCMs, using modality-specific expert streams with shared attention and positional encoding to promote geometry-layout consistency. Experiments on indoor, outdoor, synthetic, and in-the-wild scenes show that Mira-Scene substantially outperforms strong baselines in layout accuracy, achieving relative gains of 39.8% in 3D-IoU and 16.5% in 2D-IoU over SAM3D, using limited open-source training data.

潘佳老师实验室.title: LiFR v2: Completion-Augmented Event Propagation for High-Rate Dense Prediction
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Tao Wan, Xiaoshan Wu, Yifei Yu, Bo Wang, Xiaoyang Lyu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: LiFR v2 enhances high-rate dense prediction by integrating RGB keyframes and event data through a novel framework, achieving superior performance in semantic segmentation and depth estimation.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: High-rate dense perception in dynamic environments is limited by the low update rate of RGB cameras, as rapid scene changes can occur between frames. It also exceeds 100 FPS for both segmentation and depth, demonstrating accurate and efficient high-rate perception beyond RGB frame rates.

潘佳老师实验室.title: PhyVisGen: Physically and Visually High-Fidelity Robotic Manipulation Data Generation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yu Zheng, Qiyu Feng, Yixin Wu, Baoquan Yang, Yixuan Zhou
潘佳老师实验室.summary: PhyVisGen is a high-fidelity framework for generating scalable robotic manipulation data, achieving 65-95% success in real tasks using solely synthetic demonstrations.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large-scale manipulation demonstrations are essential for learning robust visuomotor policies, yet real-world data collection is expensive and difficult to scale. On the visual side, it combines real-scene reconstruction with real-time path tracing to generate visually realistic observations while preserving captured scene appearance. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate the physical and visual fidelity of PhyVisGen. Policies trained exclusively on synthetic manipulation demonstrations achieve 65-95% success across five real-robot tasks, without real-robot demonstration data or policy fine-tuning.
